pr_title: wsContainersAttach attach to stdin/out/err streams as requested
pr_body:
**- What I did**
`attach/ws` API applies stdlin/stdout/stderr parameters to select streams to attach to (as documented)
closes #43272

**- How I did it**
set parameters on `ContainerAttachConfig`. Also aligned struct initialization with `postContainersAttach` for consistency.

**- How to verify it**

curl -v -H 'Connection: upgrade' -H 'upgrade: websocket' -H 'Sec-Websocket-Key:hello' -H 'Sec-Websocket-Version: 13'tp://localhost:2375/v1.41/containers/$ID/attach/ws?stream=1&stdout=1"  --output -

**- Description for the changelog**
`containers/{ID}/attach/ws` only attach to streams according by `stdin`, `stdout` and `stderr` parameters.

**- A picture of a cute animal (not mandatory but encouraged)**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/132757/156752804-8ab3f249-190e-483e-888b-49ce0efa1baf.png)
pr_comments:
@cpuguy83 I replaced TODO with a comment, but still multiplex is set to `false`, so we don't use data multiplexing, but just plain websocket transport
The only change here is to allow clients to select the streams to be attached, so they can only attach to stdout and ignore stderr (for sample)
Thanks for clarifying, I see that now. Don't know why I didn't see that before.
I think we should keep the existing behavior for old API versions.

Yes, if this breaks current clients, we should probably make the (default) behavior depend on the API version. (Haven't looked in depth what/how things break)

Perhaps would be good to;

- describe the change in the commit message (perhaps refer to the commit that changed it, that I mentioned in https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/43272#issuecomment-1048950945 - if that's indeed the commit that broke it); FWIW; I try to avoid mentioning issue numbers in the commit message, as they can generate a lot of "noise" on github, and usually refer to _commit_ in the commit message itself - this also allows finding the change back locally (without github))
- I haven't checked what the API documentation describes currently (swagger); perhaps you can check if the documentation describes it correctly.
- same for the API version-history; https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/docs/api/version-history.md

(Happy to help with  rephrasing / wording if needed)

I've checked endpoint history, and it actually never supported streams to be selected. Initial implementation used a distinct backend function for HTTP and WS attachment, which was simplified into a single one by https://github.com/moby/moby/commit/a77b7dd2278106b9081d0ef2260fbeea790a91ef (https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/18943).
I've updated this PR accordingly:
- parameters are only used to select streams if API >= 1.42
- API change is documented
- swagger is already correct

> and it actually never supported streams to be selected. Initial implementation used a distinct backend function for HTTP and WS attachment, which was simplified into a single one by https://github.com/moby/moby/commit/a77b7dd2278106b9081d0ef2260fbeea790a91ef.

Interesting; so it didn't work before https://github.com/moby/moby/commit/c44f513248a8b40b1b2221726c7441881383e919 (https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/12120) either? https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/43272#issuecomment-1048950945
So, looks like the documentation for existing API versions is incorrect, as it mentions the `default` to be `false`; https://docs.docker.com/engine/api/v1.41/#operation/ContainerAttachWebsocket

**Description**

The [docs](https://docs.docker.com/engine/api/v1.41/#operation/ContainerAttachWebsocket) describe, that `ContainerAttachWebsocket`  is configurable for stdin/stdout/stderr, but stdin and stderr are always merged, independently of the actual params.

Possible, the reason is here:
If I followed the code correctly, 
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/7b9275c0da707b030e62c96b679a976f31f929d3/api/server/router/container/container.go#L45
links to the function wsContainersAttach
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/9e7bbdb9ba53440cfc67e2e1de89e35e44c43ddf/api/server/router/container/container_routes.go#L640
which sets stdin, stdout and stderr to true and actually ignores the params:
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/9e7bbdb9ba53440cfc67e2e1de89e35e44c43ddf/api/server/router/container/container_routes.go#L676-L685

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**

Just have a container with some stdout:
```bash
docker run ubuntu bash -c "echo 'Hello World' && sleep 1000"
```

Connecting to the container using python docker api:
```py
import docker

api_client = docker.APIClient('yourdockersocket')
# Uses /containers/{name:.*}/attach/ws (Websocket Stream)
sock = api_client.attach_socket('test_container_id', params={'stderr': 1, 'stream': 1, 'logs': 1}, ws=True)
print(sock1.read(11))
```
will output stdout as well, although only stderr is desired. On the other hand:
```py
import docker

api_client = docker.APIClient('yourdockersocket')
# Uses /containers/{name:.*}/attach (TCP stream)
sock = api_client.attach_socket('test_container_id', params={'stderr': 1, 'stream': 1, 'logs': 1})
print(sock1.read(11))
```
will correctly, probably using
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/9e7bbdb9ba53440cfc67e2e1de89e35e44c43ddf/api/server/router/container/container_routes.go#L613-L622


**Describe the results you received:**
As explained above, stderr and stdout merged stream is returned in the websocket endpoint, although not specified.

**Describe the results you expected:**
As explained above, expected result would be the stderr stream and stdout stream separately, but they are merged for the websocket request.

comments:
Thanks for reporting; having a look in git history, I _suspect_ that this is the commit where this changed; https://github.com/moby/moby/commit/c44f513248a8b40b1b2221726c7441881383e919 (https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/12120)

Or at least, I see some of the booleans being removed there, and don't see a direct replacement for those 🤔
@ndeloof  perhaps this is something to look into as well (after your other PR was merged)

review_comments:
Trying to think if there's a way to make the change less disruptive, but not sure how to;

- API < 1.41 enabled these by default (which didn't match the docs (see my other comment)), so I'd consider that to be a bug
- But has been around for a long time, so we probably shouldn't change for existing API versions

So in the old API versions; if I didn't look at the API docs, and forgot to set `?stdin=1&stdout=1&stderr=1`, then I would _still_ have all three attached.

In the new API version; I _MUST_ set all three to preserve the old behavior; which matches what was documented, but (see above) "just worked" before.


So, yeah, I don't see a clear way to migrate between one and the other, other than calling it out explicitly in the release notes 🤔 🤷‍♂️
